title: Length of a Military Service Hold Extension
content:
**Portal terms — Hardship and Protective Holds.** When a servicemember extends a running Military Service Hold, the days the service extension adds are defined as follows.

The days the service extension adds are the tier's extension days, counted from the day after the hold's current end date. The days the service extension adds are a whole number of calendar days and are not rounded. The new end date is the current end date plus the days the service extension adds.

| Quantity | Source |
|---|---|
| Extension days of the tier | The Military Service Hold's extension days in the product's schedule of hold lengths and extensions |
| Current end date | The end date shown on the hold's record |
| First day added | The day after the current end date |

## Worked example (hypothetical)

A Military Service Hold's current end date is 30 June. Taking, for the illustration, an extension-days figure of 180 calendar days, the extension is counted from 1 July and adds 180 days; the new end date is 30 June plus 180 days, that is 27 December.

## Questions answered

**From which day is the extension counted?** From the day after the hold's current end date.

**Can the figure include a fraction of a day?** No. It is a whole number of calendar days and is not rounded.
